answers.q: How many weeks of vacation does an employee with 12 years of service get?
answers.answer: An employee with 12 years of service gets 4 weeks of vacation as per the policy in force from 2024-01-01. [TOF-4@v1]

answers.q: Can unused personal sick time be carried over to the next year?
answers.answer: No, unused personal sick time cannot be carried over to the next year as per TOF-6 version v1 in force from 2024-01-01. [TOF-6@v1]

answers.q: Can supplemental employees earn personal choice holidays?
answers.answer: No, supplemental employees cannot earn personal choice holidays as per TOF-3 version v1 in force from 2024-01-01. [TOF-3@v1]

answers.q: Who must approve a 15% discount on a $12,000 deal?
answers.answer: A Sales Representative may approve a 15% discount on a $12,000 deal for Tier 2 customers according to DSC-1@v1. [DSC-1@v1] However, as of 2026-09-30, the current version of the policy does not change this requirement; thus, a Sales Representative still has the authority to approve such discounts for Tier 2 customers. [DSC-1@v1]
answers.note: Known failure: needs two rules at once (DSC-1 tier limit and DSC-2 deal size). The 7B model applied only DSC-1; correct answer: a Sales Manager, since the deal is between $5,000 and $25,000 and the discount exceeds 10%.

answers.q: What is the maximum discount a sales representative can give a Tier 3 startup customer without further approval?
answers.answer: The maximum discount a sales representative can give a Tier 3 startup customer without further approval is 10%. This was decided as per DSC-1, which is in force from 2025-01-01. [DSC-1@v1]

answers.q: What is the minimum gross margin allowed after a discount?
answers.answer: The minimum gross margin allowed after a discount is 30%, unless explicitly approved by the Vice President of Sales. [DSC-3@v1]

answers.q: What signing bonus does a newly hired First Officer pilot receive?
answers.answer: A newly hired First Officer pilot receives a one-time signing bonus of $10,000. [PAY-2.2@v1]

answers.q: What is the per diem rate for pilots on international assignments?
answers.answer: The per diem rate for pilots on international assignments is $5.00 per hour, as stated in Clause PAY-3 version v1 effective from 2025-02-01. [PAY-3@v1]

answers.q: At what amount must a single transaction be flagged for money laundering?
answers.answer: As of 2026-09-30, a single transaction must be flagged for money laundering if its amount is greater than or equal to 10,000 USD (or equivalent in any supported currency). [AML-1@v1]

answers.q: When is an account considered dormant for anti-money laundering monitoring?
answers.answer: An account is considered dormant for anti-money laundering monitoring if it has no debit or credit activity for at least 180 consecutive days. [AML-4@v1]

answers.q: When do we have to apply enhanced due diligence to a customer?
answers.answer: Enhanced due diligence (EDD) should be applied when any of the following conditions are met: The customer is a politically exposed person (PEP) or closely associated with a PEP. The transaction involves a country classified as high-risk by the EU or the FATF. The customer qualifies as a high-net-worth individual, with wealth equal to or exceeding €50 million. The transaction involves the use of auto-hosted crypto wallets or a correspondent relationship between crypto-asset service providers across borders. [CDD-2@v1] For individuals, the institution must verify the full name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, official government-issued ID, and a recent photograph. For legal entities, it must verify the registered legal name, company registration number, address, legal structure, and the identity of the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). [CDD-3@v1] The compliance system must automatically block or delay transactions when regulatory thresholds are exceeded until CDD is complete. If a customer matches a PEP list or a financial sanctions list, the system must initiate enhanced due diligence protocols and notify the compliance officer. [CDD-5@v1]

answers.q: How long must customer due diligence records be retained?
answers.answer: Customer due diligence records must be retained for a minimum of five years after the end of the business relationship or the execution of the occasional transaction, as per Clause CDD-4 version v1 in force from 2025-07-01. [CDD-4@v1]

answers.q: What does an applicant need for a personal loan to be auto-approved?
answers.answer: An applicant needs a minimum credit score of 700 and a debt-to-income ratio of 30% or lower for their personal loan to be auto-approved. [LNP-2@v1]

answers.q: What is the maximum debt-to-income ratio allowed under the US loan approval policy?
answers.answer: The maximum debt-to-income ratio allowed under the US loan approval policy is 40% as per LNU-3. [LNU-3@v1]

answers.q: What is the excess baggage fee for an oversized bag?
answers.answer: The excess baggage fee for an oversized bag is $100. [LUG-5@v1]

answers.q: Are imported electronics shipments subject to customs inspection?
answers.answer: Imported electronics shipments are subject to customs inspection if they meet certain conditions as per the Border Compliance Policy for Imported Goods. [BRD-5@v1] Specifically, inspections may be required if the goods include electronics or luxury items, are declared as such, originate from a high-risk country, or are otherwise warranted by customs enforcement criteria. [BRD-5@v1]

answers.q: By what date must annual aircraft emissions reports be submitted?
answers.answer: Annual aircraft emissions reports must be submitted by March 31st for the preceding calendar year. [ENV-1@v1]

answers.q: What happens to a cross-border transaction with a fraud risk score above 60?
answers.note: v2 in force: block and notify the compliance team
answers.answer: A cross-border transaction with a fraud risk score above 60 is blocked and notified to the compliance team. [XBF-6@v2]

answers.q: What happens to a cross-border transaction with a fraud risk score above 60?
answers.note: same question after v3 (2026-01-15): block and initiate EDD / SAR
answers.answer: A cross-border transaction with a fraud risk score above 60 is blocked and initiated for Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) / Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) process. [XBF-6@v3] Further, every flagged transaction must include Geo-IP location, Merchant jurisdiction, Currency conversion path, AML/KYC status of user, and Sanctions or watchlist match flags as per Clause XBF-7. [XBF-7@v3]

answers.q: What must be recorded for every flagged cross-border transaction?
answers.answer: Every flagged cross-border transaction must include Geo-IP location, Merchant jurisdiction, Currency conversion path, AML/KYC status of user, and Sanctions or watchlist match flags. [XBF-7@v3]
